evidence: Cic. Off. 3.92: pacta et prōmissa semperne servanda sint
Cic. Att. 6.3.1: ex pactō et conventō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: As agreed, ex pactō; to keep to an agreement, stāre pactō (Liv. 9.11, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Att. 4.18.2: pactiōnem cum aliquō facere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Rosc. Com. 34: pactiōnem facere dē aliquā rē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The making of an agreement and the agreement made: pactiōnem facere, to make a deal.

terms.gloss: a term of an agreement; terms
an agreement, a formal accord (between states)
evidence: M-O s.v. treaty: agreement, accord, convention (diplomatic)

terms.gloss: a settlement: the making up of a dispute
evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.24: pācis, concordiae, compositiōnis auctor esse nōn dēstitī
terms.comment: A peaceful accommodation, an agreement that ends a quarrel or a war (Lewis & Short); to settle a dispute is contrōversiam compōnere (M-O s.v. amicable). Its first sense is a putting together, an arrangement.

phrases.latin: Pacta et prōmissa semperne servanda sint, quae nec vī nec dolō malō, ut praetōrēs solent, facta sint.
phrases.english: Whether agreements and promises made, as the praetors put it, without force or fraud must always be kept.
the drones refuse; the bees accept the terms
